content:
mira: Heads-up — got a billing alert: ~$48k in GPU on-demand charges in the last 24h. Spike started 2026-03-17 03:12 UTC. Paging infra to help triage :eyes:
deploy-bot: alert: daily-cost-threshold breached (team=infra) — total: $47,982 — top cost: ec2:p4d.24xlarge — see: https://console.aws.amazon.com/billing/home
sam: omg, p4d? we shouldn't be running any p4d in prod. Mira, any autoscaler logs around 03:10-03:20?
mira: pasting extracted events from cluster autoscaler logs (filtered):
```
2026-03-17T03:11:22Z cluster-autoscaler: ScaleUp: triggered by pod gpu-burst-rc-0, nodegroup gpu-burst-template -> requested 42 -> provisioning using launchTemplate lt-gpu-burst:v7
2026-03-17T03:11:28Z aws: LaunchTemplate resolved instanceType: p4d.24xlarge (overrides: instanceType=null -> default from lt)
2026-03-17T03:12:05Z cluster-autoscaler: 40 nodes launched in us-east-1a (nodegroup gpu-burst-template)
2026-03-17T03:12:45Z kube-scheduler: pods scheduled to new nodes
```

mira: we intended to scale g5.2xlarge capacity (reserved commit) — the LC/template got a default instanceType bumped in a recent PR (see #3248) which apparently changed the default to p4d.24xlarge in the template v7.
alex: confirmed — PR #3248 changed the launch template default for mtu tuning tests but the variable was left unset in the roll, so lt-v7 fell back to p4d. That's on me, rolled that change during the canary last week and forgot to pin instance_type. :facepalm:
jonah: quick note on billing side: our Reserved Instances / Savings Plan commitments are scoped to g5 family (g5.2xlarge) in us-east-1 but RIs are SKU/instance type specific. p4d does not match, so usage went to on-demand — hence the big cost hit. finance-bot: invoicing note: 40 p4d.24xlarge * 24h =~ $46k/day (rough) — matches the alert.

sam: can we confirm how many nodes were provisioned and which AZs? kubectl & aws describe-ec2 please. I can also revoke scale if needed.
mira: quick outputs: `kubectl get nodes --selector=group=gpu-burst -o wide | wc -l` -> 40, AZs: us-east-1a (40). aws cli: `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=gpu-burst*" --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].[InstanceType,Placement.AvailabilityZone,State.Name]'` -> majority `p4d.24xlarge, us-east-1a, running`

alex: I'm rolling the launch-template back to lt-v6 (pinned instance_type=g5.2xlarge) now and starting a drain on the p4d nodes. Will annotate in the PR and add a guard.

jonah: please also tag those instances with billing:uncommitted so finance can fast-track a credit request & make sure cost center attribution is correct.

mira: doing node cordon+drain in waves. plan: cordon 10 nodes, wait 5m for pods to reschedule onto reserved g5 nodes (we have 120 g5 capacity reserved), then terminate the old ones. Will post progress.

sam: quick safety check — do not terminate p4d until pods are confirmed on g5s. Some jobs may prefer p4d (memory). Use `kubectl get pods -o wide` to verify.

mira: update 03:40 UTC — first 10 nodes drained and terminated, pods rescheduled, no restarts. autoscaler scaled back down to pre-spike target. Current running p4d: 6 (still draining). Estimated cost containment: ~$3k remaining for the day.

alex: opened a follow-up ticket to add Terraform validation that prevents leaving instance_type unset in LT variables + a pre-merge check to ensure launch templates match reserved SKUs.

jonah: finance will file a billing investigation with AWS for potential one-time partial credit (mislaunch due to template rollback/ops error). Also reviewing our RI/Savings Plan coverage windows — might need cross-AZ reservations or compute-savings-plan next cycle to reduce this class of mismatch.

mira: tl;dr: root cause = launch template default override (PR #3248) caused autoscaler to provision p4d instead of g5; RIs didn't apply; large on-demand spike; rollback + drain mitigated. Actions: 1) rollback + guard (done), 2) tf validation + pre-merge CI (alex), 3) billing ticket (jonah/finance), 4) review commitment strategy (cross-AZ / savings plan) — filing RFC.
sam: thanks everyone — please drop links to PR/issue IDs in this thread when available. :thumbsup:
